subject: glasswing butterfly
title: This Butterfly's Wings Reflect Only 2 Percent of Light

scenes.text: This butterfly is hiding in plain sight. You can see right through it.
Its wings are clear, but clear things still reflect light. Glass reflects a lot.
These wings reflect only about two to five percent, depending on the angle.
The secret is tiny pillars on the wing, 400 to 600 nanometers tall, in a random pattern.
The randomness is what cancels the glare. And birds find it harder to track.
It's camouflage built from physics, and engineers are copying it for lenses and screens.

description:
The glasswing butterfly has transparent wings that reflect only about two to five percent of light.
Tiny random pillars on the wings cut the glare, which helps it hide from predators.
Have you ever seen one in real life?
thumbnail_text: THE BUTTERFLY YOU CAN SEE THROUGH
